plan: This is a second-price auction format where I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying (winning at a price above my value), and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities without any benefit. This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since I win only if I'm highest, and pay the second-highest bid (not my own), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $20, so I will bid exactly $20 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value (negative profit). If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $20.
